title: Cap. III Rat. 8: if not from foresight, majority would be elect — few are saved
pass_a_gloss: Reason 8. If God should predestine without foresight of our works, he would have predestined at least the greater part of human beings to life, since he is good by nature, and his mercy is over all his works: But few are they who are saved: Therefore God does not predestine except according to foresight of works, that is of the good or bad use of free choice.
pass_b_english: Rat. 8. Without foresight of our works, they argue, a God good by nature — whose mercy is over all his works — would have marked at least most of humankind for life. Yet few are saved. So predestination must track foresight of works, that is of free choice used well or badly.
source_text: Rat. 8. Si Deus absque operum nostrorum praescientia praedestinaret, majorem saltem partem hominum praedestinasset ad vitam, cum sit natura bonus, et misericordia ejus sit super omnia opera ejus: At pauci sunt qui salvantur: Ergo non praedestinat Deus nisi secundum praevisionem operum sive boni aut mali usus liberi arbitrii.
notes: Densify De praedestinatione Cap. III Rat. 8 section 307. Pass A!=B. Packet praedestinatione_cap3_rat8_densify. Honest partial.
